title: Introduce subtrace-latency-slice-runner and rolling-baseline-bundler
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We needed a smaller-granularity benchmarking primitive that captures per-request subtraces (kernel-level and runtime-phase boundaries) and converts them into latency 'slices' that can be aggregated across sliding windows. Existing runners provide session-level metrics but obscure intra-request hotspots and transient tail contributors. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) subtrace-latency-slice-runner: a workload runner that emits compact subtrace slices per request and tags them with kernel/hotpath metadata; (2) rolling-baseline-bundler: a pipeline component that maintains rolling baselines (median/p95/p99) per slice-type and emits baseline bundles used by downstream reporters and alerting.

review_thread: Diego Ramos: Nice approach. Two things: make sure the bundler windowing supports irregular ingestion (we see bursts). Also add a lightweight sanity check to avoid baselines being poisoned by synthetic workloads.
Maya Chen (author): Added burst-tolerant reservoir sampler and a safelist to ignore synthetic markers. See new config parameters: reservoir_capacity and ignore_tags.
Anya Patel: Can you include a note on cardinality control? We have thousands of kernel-tag combinations in some experiments and that could explode memory for the rolling state.
Maya Chen: Added cardinality cap + LRU eviction and per-slice aggregation bucketing. Documented expected memory vs cardinality tradeoffs in docs/runner_integration.md.
Samir Gupta: Unit tests look good. Integration run in CI took ~14m and produced stable bundles. Approving pending a small nits fix in README.
Samir Gupta: nit: quickstart command missing --output-dir flag (fixed in last commit).

release_notes: Introduce a new subtrace-level runner and a rolling baseline bundler to capture intra-request hotspots and maintain sliding-window baselines. Useful for kernel-level attribution and alerting on slice regressions. Backward compatible with existing reporters.
